senses.gloss: m. (קְטַר I) knot, band.—Pl. קִיטְרִין, קִיטְרֵי, קִטְ׳, קוּטְ׳. Targ. II Esth. VI, 10 קִ׳ חרציה וכ׳ (some ed. קַ׳, v.
units: <cite ref="Daniel 5:6">Dan. V, 6</cite>) the knots of (the belt of) his loins were loosed, v. <cite ref="S00726"><he>קְטוֹר</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Chullin 51a:12">Ib. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>אי אית ביה ק׳</he> if the stick is knotty (has hard protuberances).
<cite ref="Pesachim 74a:4">Pes. 74ᵃ</cite> <he>שיעי ק׳</he> (Ms. O. <he>קיטריה</he>, Rashi <he>קוטריה</he>) the knots on the branch of a pomegranate tree are smooth.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 7:2:8">Y. Shek. VII, beg. 50ᶜ</cite> <he>יחכמון … קִיטְרֵיהוֹן</he> let the wine sellers identify their knots (made as seals, v. <cite ref="H00498"><he>חוֹתָם</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Ketubot 93a">Keth. 93ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>חייתא דק׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H00747"><he>חַיְיתָא</he> IV</cite>; a. fr.—Trnsf.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 7:18">Targ. Is. VII, 18</cite> (?).—
senses.label: a

units: <cite ref="Yevamot 107b:9">Yeb. 107ᵇ</cite> <he>תרי ק׳ עבדו ביה</he> they put him under two disadvantages.
